gen.title: How Lift Relates to Area and Motion

cards.stem: What happens to lift when the wing area is enlarged and other factors remain the same
options: Doubling the area doubles the lift
Lift stays constant when area changes
cards.quote: Like the other aerodynamic force, drag, the lift is directly proportional to the area of the object. Doubling the area doubles the lift.
cards.hint: Recall the direct proportion described for lift and area

cards.stem: How is lift oriented relative to the direction of flight
options: toward the ground at all times
cards.quote: Lift is the component of this force perpendicular to the flight direction.
cards.hint: Think about lift as a named component of aerodynamic force

cards.stem: What combination produces the total aerodynamic force on a body moving through air
cards.quote: The total aerodynamic force is equal to the pressure times the surface area around the body.
cards.hint: Focus on how pressure and surface area combine

cards.stem: What action helps keep lift high when velocity is low during takeoff and landing
cards.quote: Takeoff and landing are times of relatively low velocity, so to keep the lift high (to avoid the ground!) designers try to increase the wing area.
cards.hint: Remember what designers do when velocity is relatively low
